newsitem.title: KENYA: Sudan president, rebels differ over peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Sudan president, rebels differ over peace talks.

text.p: Sudan's president said he accepted on Wednesday a framework of principles for talks to end Sudan's civil war as not binding on both parties but a basis for discussion.
In response to President Omar Hassan al-Bashir's statement, a spokesman for the largest rebel group in Sudan told Reuters it would not reopen peace talks if the president stuck to his position.

"It is only a basis for discussion and negotiations and is not a binding description," Bashir told a news conference before quoting from a summit statement saying that the declaration of principles was "the basis for discussions and negotiations".

Bashir said when Khartoum refused to accept the declaration of principles in September 1994 and Nairobi peace talks broke down, it was "the understanding at that time that the principles were obigatory and binding to the parties to the conflict".
"Now following intensive consultations and deliberations by the summit, this thing has been redefined as a basis for negotiations and discussion," added the Sudanese president.

But George Benjamin, a spokesman for the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) led by John Garang said: "We will not go to talks if Bashir sticks to his position that the declaration of principles is not binding.
"The government must commit itself and be bound by these principles as well as the outcome of negotiations," he added.
